general_conventions: Marks use OCR's MACB categories: B = independent mark that must be explicitly seen; M = method mark on which A marks depend; C = compensatory method mark that can be credited if later correct working implies it; A = accuracy/answer mark dependent on M or C.

Conventions: '/' separates alternative acceptable answers; reject/not = not creditworthy; ignore = irrelevant; allow = acceptable; bracketed words are not required; underlined words are essential; ECF = error carried forward; AW = alternative wording; ORA = or reverse argument.
Significant figures: with 2 s.f. data, answers to 2 or more s.f. are accepted; giving fewer than 2 s.f. is penalised only once in the whole paper unless the guidance states an exception.

On-screen marking annotations include benefit of doubt (BOD), contradiction (CON), ECF, POT (power-of-ten error), SF (significant-figure error), TE (transcription error), XP (wrong physics or equation), omission mark, and L1/L2/L3 level markers.
Section A: 20 multiple-choice items at 1 mark each (letter only); Section B: structured questions worth 50 marks; total 70.
Values in brackets in the answer column (e.g. units) need not be written when the unit is printed on the answer line; 'any subject' means the equation may be rearranged in any form for the C mark.
